subject: Post-demo pricing + deployment follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>; Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo pricing + deployment follow-up — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private

Hi Lena / Carlos —

Thanks for joining today’s demo. Quick recap and the specific asks we discussed so you have everything in one place. Appreciate the clarity on Acme’s primary constraints: sensitive PII indexing workloads, multi-hour peek traffic spikes around month-end, and a desire for predictable monthly spend for budgeting.

Summary of deployment options we walked through (high level):
- Hosted API (Redwood managed): Fastest to ship, usage-based billing (per-token). Good for variable workloads and low ops overhead.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): GPU pools dedicated to Acme with monthly reserved commits + burst capacity. Predictable throughput and unit cost; better for steady, high-throughput inference.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): Customer-managed network and control plane. Best for strict compliance or air-gapped needs; typically larger upfront infra/enablement costs but lowest long-term per-token costs at scale.

Action items we agreed:
1) I’ll send a simple pricing model comparing per-token costs vs committed capacity economics + an estimated commit recommendation based on your month-end peaks (attached: ACME_pricing_model_v1.xlsx).
2) Monica will follow up with a short TCO sketch for Private VPC including one-time setup and typical infra ranges.
3) Provide SOC2 and network requirements doc (attached).

Next meeting: Wed 3/11 10:00am PT to review the numbers and pick a recommended approach. If that works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Open questions (for Acme):
- Preferred contracting cadence: monthly or annual commits?
- Are you comfortable with partial offload to Hosted for non-sensitive workloads as a hybrid approach?
- Any SSO/KMS constraints we should model now?

Thanks —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0124
redwood.com

Thanks Jordan — very helpful summary and thanks for the spreadsheet. A couple quick clarifications before the deep review:

1) For our month-end spike: today it’s roughly 8 hours at 4–6x baseline traffic. Is the committed capacity recommendation in the spreadsheet designed to cover that peak, or should we expect burst throttling?

2) On private deployment: security will need the full network diagram and a KMS/HSM integration plan. Can you provide a short note on what Redwood needs from our side and an estimated lead time for an on-prem setup?

3) Contracting: we prefer annual commits for budget predictability but want an option to scale up for 2 quarters if needed. Are flexible commit top-ups supported mid-term?

We’ll aim to have Procurement looped in for the Wed review.

—Lena
Head of Product Operations, Acme Analytics

Hi Lena — quick answers inline then Monica and I will expand in the Wed review: 

1) Month-end spikes: the attached model includes two recommendation rows — "steady-commit" sized for baseline throughput and "peak-buffer" that covers 95th percentile month-end spikes. Dedicated with a modest buffer (20–30% above baseline) plus burst capacity is our recommended sweet spot if you need zero throttling. Hosted can handle spikes but at variable per-token cost; we show both in the workbook.

2) Private/VPC lead time: typical timeline is 6–10 weeks for VPC with Redwood-managed control plane + KMS integrations. On-prem (air-gapped) is 10–14 weeks and requires an on-site infra partner. I’ve attached SOC2 and a simple diagram; Monica will draft the itemized requirements.

3) Flexible top-ups: yes — we support mid-term commit increases. We also offer a graduated pricing ladder for increases within a 90-day window so you don't pay full incremental list for immediately added capacity. Details in the pricing tab of the workbook.

I’ll put a short note below with the three pricing scenarios so Procurement has a bullet view before Wed.

Jordan

---
Three short scenarios (high level) — ballpark monthly run-rate estimates (USD, illustrative):

- Scenario A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go): 0.35–0.65 per 1k tokens depending on model family and streaming vs non-streaming. No commit; operationally simplest. Good if you value time-to-market and episodic usage.

- Scenario B — Dedicated (reserved capacity): committed monthly GPU pool. Typical pricing: $12k–$40k per reserved GPU/month depending on instance type and model; effective per-1k-token cost falls to ~$0.05–0.20 at steady state for high-throughput workloads. We show an example commit sized for your 4–6x peak and the amortized token cost in the spreadsheet.

- Scenario C — Private VPC / On-prem: higher up-front enablement ($30k–$120k professional services + infra), ongoing infra + ops. At large sustained volume, per-1k-token cost can be <$0.04 but requires a multi-quarter payback.

Notes/assumptions: all figures exclude applicable discounts and network egress; we’ll model exact numbers once we have the monthly token estimate and preferred commit window.

Attachments referenced: ACME_pricing_model_v1.xlsx (sent with this thread).

Jordan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Internal: Prep notes for Wed ACME review (pricing + security asks)

Internal — quick prep for our 3/11 session with Acme. Pulling together the short TCO and the VPC checklist. Key bullets to bring: 

- Bring three canonical slides: 1) cost comparison table (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 2) recommended commit sizing with sensitivity to month-end spikes, 3) security checklist + docs/attestations.
- For commit sizing: propose a conservative starting commit equating to ~2.5x baseline (covers most of spike in sample logs) with a 30% burst pool. This keeps effective per-token cost in the "Dedicated" row at the favorable part of the ladder while limiting upfront spend.
- For Procurement Qs: draft contract language for annual commit with mid-term top-ups and a 60-day exit/scale window for downsizing after first year.
- KMS/HSM: need to confirm if Acme will provision a customer-managed KMS key or wants Redwood-managed key escrow. If Acme wants HSM-backed keys on their side, we’ll include PS estimate.

Attach to the invite: ACME_pricing_model_v1.xlsx, SOC2_certificate.pdf, Private_VPC_arch_diagram.png.

I’ll circulate the slide pack and a short one-pager TCO this afternoon so Jordan can drop the invite.

—Monica
